questions.q: When testing whether (|00⟩+|01⟩+|10⟩−|11⟩)/2 is entangled, matching coefficients against (a|0⟩+b|1⟩)⊗(c|0⟩+d|1⟩) requires ac=1/2, ad=1/2, bc=1/2, bd=−1/2. What contradiction does this produce?
options: The state turns out not to be normalized
ac=1/2 and ad=1/2 force d=c, while bc=1/2 and bd=−1/2 force d=−c; together these force d=0 (or c=0), which then contradicts ad=1/2 (or ac=1/2) being nonzero
There is no contradiction — the state factors cleanly with a=b=c=d=1/2
The equations require a and b to both be zero simultaneously
questions.explain: Dividing ad/ac=1 gives d=c; dividing bd/bc=-1 gives d=-c. Both can only hold if d=c=0, but that makes ad or ac equal 0, contradicting their required value of 1/2. No consistent a,b,c,d exists, so the state is entangled.

questions.q: The Bell state |Ψ+⟩ = (|01⟩+|10⟩)/√2 produces what measurement pattern, in contrast to |Φ+⟩'s pattern from lesson 17?
options: The same pattern as |Φ+⟩: P(00)=P(11)=0.5, P(01)=P(10)=0
Perfect anti-correlation: P(01)=P(10)=0.5 and P(00)=P(11)=0 — the two qubits always measure opposite values rather than the same value
Completely uncorrelated: all four outcomes equally likely at 0.25 each
Qubit 1 always measures 0 with certainty
questions.explain: Because the surviving terms after measuring qubit 1 are |01⟩ (if qubit 1 is 0, qubit 2 is 1) or |10⟩ (if qubit 1 is 1, qubit 2 is 0), |Ψ+⟩ gives perfect anti-correlation rather than |Φ+⟩'s perfect same-value correlation.

questions.q: A colleague argues that because a local hidden-variable script can perfectly reproduce |Φ+⟩'s single-basis correlation numbers, entanglement must be 'nothing special.' What is the precise flaw in this argument?
options: There is no flaw — they are completely correct and lesson 19's result doesn't change anything

The flaw is that single-basis correlation genuinely cannot distinguish entanglement from a classical script, but once measurements are taken at multiple different angles (the CHSH setup), the entangled pair's |S|=2√2≈2.828 exceeds the classical bound of |S|≤2 that any hidden-variable script is limited to
The flaw is that classical coins can never produce any correlation at all, so the comparison itself is invalid
The flaw is that |Φ+⟩ cannot actually be measured in the computational basis
questions.explain: The colleague is right about the single-basis case — that's exactly the honest part of the objection lesson 18 took seriously. The resolution is the multi-basis CHSH test from lesson 19: no classical script can exceed |S|=2, while the entangled pair measurably reaches 2√2, which is the real, checkable distinction.

questions.q: Why is it incorrect to say that measuring qubit 1 of |Φ+⟩ sends information faster than light to qubit 2?
options: Because entanglement doesn't actually produce any correlation, so there's nothing to transmit

Because nothing detectable changes at qubit 2's location from measuring qubit 1 alone — qubit 2's own measurement statistics are unaffected on their own, and comparing the two results to see the correlation requires ordinary, slower-than-light communication between observers
Because qubit 2 is measured before qubit 1 in every valid experiment
Because the no-signaling principle only applies to classical particles, not qubits
questions.explain: An observer holding only qubit 2 sees unchanged 50/50 statistics regardless of what happens to qubit 1 — there is no local, detectable signal. The correlation only becomes apparent once the two measurement results are physically brought together and compared, which cannot happen faster than light. This is the no-signaling principle.

questions.q: What is the general strategy this lab lesson reinforces for determining whether any given two-qubit state is entangled?
options: Count the number of terms in the superposition — more terms always means more entangled
Check whether the state 'looks complicated' at a glance

Write the general product-state ansatz (a|0⟩+b|1⟩)⊗(c|0⟩+d|1⟩), expand it, match coefficients against the given state, and determine whether a consistent solution for a,b,c,d exists (product state) or leads to a contradiction (entangled)
Measure the state many times and see if the outcomes are ever repeated
questions.explain: Every problem in this lab used the same mechanical procedure first introduced in lesson 16: set up the product-state ansatz, expand, match coefficients, and check for a consistent solution. This is the reliable, general-purpose test — term count or 'complexity' by eye is not a valid shortcut.
